$comment: Neutral shipped <sys/file.h> (Darwin/BSD), added by the SQLite-CLI-for-arm64-Darwin cycle. ★ THE REAL HEADER IS ALMOST A PURE RE-INCLUDE SHELL, AND THE 'ALMOST' MATTERS. MEASURED line-by-line against MacOSX26.4.sdk (read-only at /tmp/apple_sdk_probe/MacOSX26.4.sdk/usr/include; nothing copied into this repo): outside the license block, sys/file.h contains its include guard, six #includes (:67-72 — sys/appleapiopts.h, sys/types.h, sys/fcntl.h, sys/unistd.h, sys/queue.h, sys/cdefs.h), an EMPTY __BEGIN_DECLS/__END_DECLS pair (it declares NO function of its own), and exactly one block of real content: the _KAUTH_CRED_T pair `struct ucred; typedef struct ucred *kauth_cred_t;` + `struct posix_cred; typedef struct posix_cred *posix_cred_t;`. That pair IS shipped below, as opaque named-struct pointers (the stdio.json `struct "FILE" {}` / dirent.json DIR precedent) — member access on one fails loud, which is the correct behaviour for a type whose body the SDK deliberately withholds. ★ THE LOCK_* FAMILY IS NOT sys/file.h's OWN CONTENT — it arrives through the sys/fcntl.h re-include, MEASURED at sys/fcntl.h:485-489 (`/* lock operations for flock(2) */` then LOCK_SH 0x01, LOCK_EX 0x02, LOCK_NB 0x04, LOCK_UN 0x08). ALL FOUR SHIP even though sqlite touches only LOCK_EX/LOCK_NB/LOCK_UN: the domain is closed and four rows wide, and a partial constant domain — a name that exists in the real header, is absent here, and so compiles to a fail-loud miss on a shadowed include — is the exact trap this project keeps re-hitting. WHY THEY ARE DECLARED HERE RATHER THAN IN fcntl.json: this cycle owns sys/file.json and does not own fcntl.json, so the rows land at the point of use. THE COST IS REAL AND IS ANCHORED: under DSS `#include <fcntl.h>` alone does NOT yield LOCK_*, whereas on real Darwin it does. D-FFI-DARWIN-LOCK-CONSTANT-PROVENANCE. ★ `includes: [fcntl.h]` REPRODUCES the one re-include that matters (the closure walker's mechanism, inttypes.json:6 → stdint.h is the precedent): DSS's fcntl.json IS the <sys/fcntl.h> surface (Darwin's <fcntl.h> is a thin shell over it), so a program that includes only <sys/file.h> and then calls open() with an O_* flag behaves as it does on Apple. MEASURED this cycle: with the closure in place, `open("/tmp/x", O_RDONLY)` compiles clean for arm64:macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from a <sys/file.h>-only include. The other five re-includes are NOT reproduced: sys/appleapiopts.h / sys/queue.h / sys/cdefs.h have no DSS descriptor and no consumer, and <sys/unistd.h> is DELIBERATELY not mapped to unistd.json — they are different headers. Apple's <sys/unistd.h> publishes only SEEK_*/F_OK-R_OK-W_OK-X_OK and the _POSIX_* limits, NOT read/write/close, so routing it to DSS's full unistd.json would OVER-supply the include and let a program compile against names real Darwin would have rejected there — a fidelity error in the direction that hides bugs. Tracked at D-FFI-DARWIN-SYS-UNISTD-SUBHEADER. ★ SHADOWING IS TOTAL (include_path_resolve.hpp:60-75, Descriptor → Source → NotFound), so this file also takes over on a NATIVE macOS host, where the SDK header is used today via D-INCLUDE-ANGLE-SOURCE-FALLBACK — hence the completeness argument above is about every consumer, not about sqlite. ★ NO `symbols` AND NO `library` KEY: DSS EAGER-IMPORTS every function a descriptor lists, so an unexported name breaks EVERY binary's LOAD (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT, macho exit 127), and every function reachable from this header is ALREADY shipped and ALREADY export-verified by a real dlopen+dlsym run on an actual Mac ([[D-LK-SQLITE-MACHO-UNDEFINED-LIBSYSTEM-SYMBOLS]]) — a second declaration would be a second eager import of the same name for no gain. Including this header therefore imports nothing. THE GAP THAT LEAVES, stated rather than hidden and MEASURED this cycle: `flock` is prototyped at sys/fcntl.h:616, so on real Darwin it reaches a caller through <sys/file.h> — but DSS files it under unistd.json:39, so a DSS program that includes only <sys/file.h> and calls flock() gets S0001 (verified: that is the one and only diagnostic this cycle's <sys/file.h> probe produced, and it disappears once <unistd.h> is included). Fail-loud, not silent, and anchored at D-FFI-DARWIN-FLOCK-PROVENANCE. Gated availableObjectFormats:[macho] — an elf/pe #include fails loud (the windows.json:5 [pe] precedent, inverted); Linux's <sys/file.h> is a different header and glibc's LOCK_* must not silently borrow these rows.
